items.title: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2026 draft adds Agentic Tool Misuse
items.description: The 2026 draft of the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications introduces a new category, Agentic Tool Misuse, covering agents that are manipulated into calling connected tools in unintended ways. It sits alongside the existing prompt injection and insecure output handling entries rather than replacing them. The category was added after multiple independent research groups reported similar confused-deputy patterns in tool-calling agents over the past two quarters.
items.consequences: Applications built with agent frameworks that don't validate tool-call intent may act outside the user's actual request, from unintended purchases to unauthorized data access.
items.remediation: OWASP recommends explicit allow-lists for tool scopes, human confirmation for high-impact actions, and logging tool-call chains for post-hoc review.

items.title: Indirect prompt injection via shared calendar invites bypasses RAG guardrails
items.description: A researcher demonstrated that a calendar invite description field can be used to smuggle instructions into a retrieval-augmented assistant. When the assistant later summarizes the event for the user, it silently follows the embedded instructions instead of treating them as untrusted data. The technique bypassed keyword-based guardrails because the payload was split across multiple event fields.
items.consequences: In the disclosed proof of concept, the assistant exfiltrated the user's upcoming meeting details to an attacker-controlled URL embedded in the invite.
items.remediation: Vendor patched by treating all retrieved third-party content as untrusted input and stripping URL-like instructions before passing content to the model.

items.title: Detecting jailbreaks via activation-space anomaly scoring
items.description: Researchers propose scoring a model's internal activations against a baseline distribution to flag jailbreak attempts before a response is generated. The method adds a lightweight classifier on top of intermediate layers rather than relying solely on output-text filtering. Reported latency overhead was under 8 milliseconds per request in their benchmark setup.
items.consequences: Not applicable -- this is a defensive research contribution rather than an incident.
items.remediation: The paper's method itself is the remediation: activation-space anomaly detection as an additional jailbreak-detection layer alongside prompt and output filtering.

items.title: CVE-2026-31337: Actively exploited deserialization flaw in enterprise VPN appliance
items.description: CISA added an unauthenticated deserialization vulnerability in a widely deployed enterprise VPN appliance to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. The flaw allows an attacker to send a crafted object to the appliance's management interface and achieve remote code execution without valid credentials. CISA confirmed active exploitation against internet-facing appliances prior to the advisory.
items.attack_source: Unattributed opportunistic scanning campaigns (per CISA advisory)
items.consequences: Successful exploitation grants full control of the VPN appliance, potentially exposing the internal network behind it.
items.remediation: Vendor released a patch; CISA's required action is to patch by the binding operational directive deadline or disconnect the appliance from the internet.

items.title: Healthcare claims processor discloses breach affecting 2.1 million patients
items.description: A healthcare claims processor disclosed that an unpatched insecure direct object reference (IDOR) in its patient portal allowed sequential enumeration of claims records by manipulating a URL parameter. The flaw had been present for approximately eight months before detection. The company has notified affected patients and state regulators as required.
items.attack_source: Unknown; discovered via third-party security research disclosure
items.consequences: Names, dates of birth, and diagnosis codes for 2.1 million patients were exposed to anyone who could guess or iterate the record identifier.
items.remediation: The company added object-level authorization checks on the claims endpoint and rotated all record identifiers to non-sequential UUIDs.
items.losses: Estimated $38M in remediation, notification, and regulatory costs (company disclosure)

items.title: OWASP Top 10:2025 Software Supply Chain Failures category gets expanded guidance
items.description: OWASP published expanded guidance for the Software Supply Chain Failures category introduced in the 2025 Top 10 refresh. The update clarifies how SBOM verification and build-pipeline attestation map onto the category's sub-risks, and adds worked examples for CI/CD dependency confusion attacks.
items.consequences: Organizations relying on the prior, thinner guidance may have under-scoped their supply-chain controls.
items.remediation: Adopt SBOM generation in CI, verify build provenance (e.g. SLSA), and pin dependency versions with hash verification.

items.title: Ransomware crew shifts to double-extortion via exposed CI/CD secrets
items.description: Investigators report a rise in ransomware initial access gained through leaked CI/CD pipeline credentials rather than phishing. Attackers scan public code repositories and misconfigured build logs for exposed tokens, then use them to pivot directly into cloud infrastructure, shortening the time from initial access to extortion demand.
items.attack_source: Multiple ransomware-as-a-service affiliates (unattributed to a single group)
items.consequences: Victims skip the usual weeks-long dwell time typical of phishing-based intrusions, leaving less time for detection before data is exfiltrated and encrypted.
items.remediation: Rotate CI/CD secrets regularly, use short-lived tokens, scan repos and build logs for accidental credential exposure, and enforce least-privilege scopes on pipeline service accounts.
items.losses: Multiple victim organizations reported six-figure ransom demands (aggregate trend reporting)

items.title: Why 'don't paste secrets into the chatbot' isn't enough anymore
items.description: As AI agents gain the ability to browse the web and read connected documents autonomously, secrets can leak even when no human manually pastes them into a prompt. The post walks through several real cases where an agent picked up credentials from a connected file store or an open browser tab and included them in a later response.
items.consequences: Traditional 'don't share sensitive data with the chatbot' training for employees no longer covers the actual risk surface once agents have autonomous access to connected systems.
items.remediation: Scope agent permissions narrowly, redact secrets at the data-source level rather than relying on prompt discipline, and audit what an agent's connected tools can actually read.

items.title: Benchmarking tool-use agents against a taxonomy of confused-deputy attacks
items.description: The paper adapts the classic confused-deputy attack pattern to agent tool-calling and introduces a benchmark of 40 scenarios. Testing against several popular open-source agent frameworks, the authors found most could be tricked into performing actions outside the user's original intent when a malicious tool description was introduced.
items.attack_source: N/A (academic benchmark, not an in-the-wild attack)
items.consequences: Frameworks that don't validate tool descriptions against expected behavior are vulnerable to being redirected into unintended actions by any tool in their toolchain.
items.remediation: The authors recommend sandboxing tool descriptions, verifying tool provenance, and adding an intent-consistency check before executing high-impact tool calls.

items.title: New Burp Suite extension automates JWT algorithm-confusion testing
items.description: A new open-source Burp Suite extension automates switching between RS256 and HS256 signing during manual testing, catching algorithm-confusion vulnerabilities in JWT implementations faster than manual Repeater workflows. It also flags endpoints that accept the 'none' algorithm.
items.consequences: Not applicable -- this is a testing tool release.
items.remediation: N/A -- the tool itself is used to find and remediate algorithm-confusion flaws before attackers do.

items.title: Retail chain point-of-sale malware campaign linked to card data theft
items.description: A point-of-sale malware campaign targeting a mid-size retail chain's payment terminals was discovered after unusual outbound traffic was flagged by the chain's fraud team. The malware scraped card data from terminal memory before encryption completed and exfiltrated it in small batches to blend in with normal traffic.
items.consequences: Card data for an estimated 400,000 transactions across 60 store locations was exposed over a six-week period before detection.
items.remediation: The chain deployed point-to-point encryption on all terminals and segmented the POS network from the corporate network.
items.losses: Estimated $12M in fraud liability, forensics, and card-reissuance costs

items.title: CVE-2026-30012
items.description: An authentication bypass was disclosed in a popular open-source API gateway. A malformed Authorization header causes the gateway to fall through to a default-allow code path, letting requests reach upstream services without valid credentials. No known exploitation in the wild has been confirmed at time of publication.
items.consequences: Any service placed behind the affected gateway version without additional authentication is reachable by unauthenticated requests.
items.remediation: Upgrade to the patched gateway version; as a stopgap, reject requests with malformed Authorization headers at the load balancer.

items.title: Manufacturing firm loses $6M in business email compromise scheme
items.description: A manufacturing firm's finance team wired $6M to a fraudulent account after receiving emails that closely mimicked an existing supplier's invoicing thread. Investigators believe the attackers had read access to the supplier's mailbox for several weeks before sending the fraudulent invoice.
items.consequences: Direct financial loss of $6M, with only a portion recoverable through the bank's fraud-reversal process.
items.remediation: The firm implemented out-of-band verification for any change to payment instructions and added DMARC enforcement to reduce email spoofing.
